data.long_meaning: Derived from the Roman family name Damianus, meaning 'tamed, subdued'. In Christianity, Damian is the name of several saints who have shown great strength and courage. The name Damianus carries the meaning “Tamed, subdued” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Damianus usually hope their child will grow to embody tamed, subdued and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes overcoming challenges and staying strong in faith.

data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Damianus total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

in_hebrew.name: דָמִיאָנוּס
in_hebrew.long_meaning: דָמִיאָנוּס, שְׁמוֹ שֶׁל אָחִיוּ דּמֶא, פּעַל-הִגְזֵר, מְשָׁפָט שֶׁל עַם יְהוּדָּה. בּעַל-כָּרֶךְ, הָיָה דָמִיאָנוּס, מְשָׁפָט שֶׁל עַם יְהוּדָּה, וְזֶה-אֲחִיוּ דּמֶא, פּעַל-הִגְזֵר.

in_greek.name: Δαμιανός
in_greek.long_meaning: Δαμιανός, όνομα του αδελφού μου Δαμιανού, έτερος δίκαιος του έθνους του Ιουδαίου. Ήταν Δαμιανός, δίκαιος του έθνους του Ιουδαίου, και ο αδελφός του Δαμιανός, έτερος δίκαιος.

in_latin.name: Damianus
in_latin.long_meaning: Damianus, nomen fratris mei Damiani, alius justus populi Iudaei. Fuit Damianus justus populi Iudaei, et frater eius Damianus, alius justus.

in_english.name: Damianus
in_english.meaning: judgment of the people of Judah, just and righteous
in_english.long_meaning: Damianus, a name of my brother Damian, another righteous one of the people of Judah. Damianus was a judgment of the people of Judah, and my brother Damian was another righteous one. The name Damianus is derived from the Hebrew name Demian, meaning 'judgment of the people of Judah'. In Christian tradition, Damian is a name associated with Saint Damian, a 3rd-century martyr and companion of Saint Cosmas. Damianus is also a variant of the name Demian, which has been used in various cultures and contexts.

data.cultural_impact: The name Damianus has its roots in ancient Rome, where it was a common surname implying control or mastery. Throughout history, numerous individuals with this name have made significant contributions to their societies. For instance, during the Middle Ages, St. Damian of Oplona, a hermit known for his simple lifestyle and devotion to God, spread Christianity throughout Italy. Moreover, St. Damian of Molokai, also known as the 'Father of the Lepers,' is recognized for ministering to the lepers in Hawaii, demonstrating compassion and selflessness. In the modern era, the name Damian can still be found in various cultures, reminding us of the societal value placed on strength, courage, and determination.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name Damianus stems from its association with the saints who have carried the name throughout history. These individuals have demonstrated exceptional faith and dedication to God, often showcasing remarkable courage and selflessness. For example, St. Damian of Oplona lived as a hermit, dedicating his life to prayer and penance. Meanwhile, St. Damian of Molokai chose to minister to the outcast lepers, nursing them back to health and providing them with spiritual guidance. These stories serve as inspirations to us all, encapsulating the importance of faith, compassion, and perseverance in the face of adversity. Additionally, the name Damianus reminds us of the divine gift of being able to tame and subdue our passions and desires, allowing us to live in harmony with God's will.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Damianus: A devoted servant of God, bearing the cross of suffering and affliction in imitation of St. Damian, the patron saint of the sick and plague-stricken. His name means "to tame" or "to subdue," symbolizing the triumph of the spirit over physical hardships.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Damianus was a 4th century Syrian ascetic and bishop, known for his extreme austerity and miracles. The name Damianus carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
